pageCache.pageTitle: Semley CE VA Primary School - Visions and Values
pageCache.text:
Visions and Values
VISION
Rooted and Growing in Love:
A culture of kindness in which all can flourish.
At Semley School we seek to offer an inspiring environment. Grounded by our vision of God's nurturing love, our children are encouraged to be confident in their own worth and to respond by respecting and caring for others, choosing to be the person who makes a difference while enjoying their learning and achieving their full potential.
VALUES
RESPECT ASPIRATION ADVENTURE WONDER
'Respect' represents the Christian values of love, kindness, and service to God and to others.
'Aspiration' represents the message of Jesus to go out into the world and make the best of the gifts we have been given and to use them for good.
'Adventure' encourages children to challenge themselves and not to be afraid, knowing that God is with them.
'Wonder' represents the unfathomable, the unknowable and the spirit of God within us and around us.
Semley Church of England School aims to be:
Building on this stable foundation we aim to:
We recognize and value the shared responsibility we have for the children of Semley School. We aim to work with others; parents, friends, supporting agencies and those who contribute to children's time outside school, in a spirit of mutual respect and trust, for the benefit of children. Thank you for visiting!

pageCache.pageTitle: Semley CE VA Primary School - Welcome
pageCache.text:
Welcome
Welcome to the Semley CE VA School website.
At Semley we firmly believe that every child is unique and we take time to value their particular gifts and talents, this includes celebrating diversity, individuality and creativity.
Semley encourages and gives opportunities for each child to shine, to achieve the best they can and to primarily enjoy their learning.
Semley CE VA Primary School is committed to providing a broad and balanced range of experiences and opportunities whilst children are in a caring and nurturing environment. The curriculum, whilst focusing on the core skills of literacy and numeracy, gives opportunities that are broad and balanced.
They learn discrete subject knowledge through carefully planned curriculum progression alongside a topic-based creative curriculum, this allows children to make meaningful links across the subjects.
At Semley we have high expectations of behaviour and attitude to learning, allowing children to develop self-respect and respect for others in the community. Our aim is that children will leave Semley as well-rounded individuals who have the confidence and skills necessary to face new challenges. We value the ideas and opinions of our children and feel giving them a voice about the things that happen at their school is important. We encourage our children to take responsibility for themselves while at the same time thinking of the impact actions may have on others, for example they have organised fundraising events for charities and instigated changes that have positively impacted playtimes and lunch times.
We are proud of our Christian ethos at Semley and the core school values: ‘aspiration,’ ‘respect,’ ‘adventure’ and ‘wonder’ are used to inspire each child to make the most of any opportunities that come their way.
I am so excited and honoured to be the Head Teacher at Semley CE VA Primary School and enjoy being part of the school’s onward journey. I hope the website can give you an insight into the busy and happy school we have here. If you would like any further information please don’t hesitate to contact us. If you would like to come and see for yourself then I am very happy to show you around.
Abi Carlyle-Clarke Headteacher
Pupils believe their school is a warm, friendly, ‘family’ school. They are respectful and kind towards one another. Pupils are resilient in their efforts to learn. They strive to work hard for their teachers. For example, children in Reception worked studiously together to create a bug hotel. Pupils say teachers show them ‘how to be’.
Pupils fully take part in school as sports ambassadors, play leaders and members of the school council. Pupils feel staff listen to their views and take them seriously. Pupil librarians listen to younger pupils read. Older pupils care for the younger children. For example, during lunchtime, pupils help to cut food or open packets for the younger children. All of this contributes to a warm, nurturing community.

pageCache.pageTitle: Semley CE VA Primary School - Breakfast Club and After School Provision
pageCache.text:
Breakfast Club and After School Provision
Breakfast Club
Our Breakfast Club runs every weekday morning from 8am. Children can be dropped off at anytime between 8.00 and 8.30.
We offer the option of a breakfast of toast, cereal and a drink, and there is a range of games and activities to keep the children busy until school starts.
The cost of Breakfast Club is £2.50 per session. This is a flat rate regardless of time of arrival and whether or not breakfast is required, and is payable weekly via ParentPay.
Please email the office (admin@semley.wilts.sch.uk) to book a place in advance. Unfortunately refunds cannot be given if the child is absent for any reason.
We allow last minute bookings on the day for unexpected events.

pageCache.pageTitle: Semley CE VA Primary School - Our Governors
pageCache.text:
Our Governors
We are a board of 9 dedicated individuals comprising members of the school community, church, staff and parents. Achieving the best possible experiences and outcomes for all children at Semley School lies at the heart of what we do and is our guiding principle in all our decisions. Along with the headteacher, we set the strategic vision of the school, ensure the finances are well managed, the curriculum is delivered, performance and progress is monitored, the best staff are recruited, the Christian ethos is upheld, policies are approved and the buildings are looked after.
We have full governing body meetings twice a term and all governors serve on at least one of the three sub committees which also meet six times a year – these are:
1. Finance - This committee monitors the school’s budget and the impact of the school’s use of Pupil Premium, COVID-Catch-Up and Sports funding. The Chairs of this committee is Lou Smith & Molly Swann.
2. Curriculum, Staffing and Admissions - This committee reviews the school’s progress with the teaching and learning action plan and all matters to do with the content and delivery of the curriculum. This committee keeps a watching brief on assessment, and the outcomes for students in national assessments as well as staffing and wellbeing. The Chair of this committee is Molly Swann.
3. Premises - This committee reviews the school’s provision for the safety, in all senses, of the staff and pupils. This committee looks at the physical aspects of the school and Health and Safety issues. The chair of this committee is Antony Pinsent.
Governors bring to the role a wide range of skills, backgrounds and interests. We know the school well, visit regularly and attend training sessions to keep up to date with the ever changing world of education. As a body, to approve the longer term development planning of the school and to monitor the realisation of those plans in the day to day workings of the school and in the outcomes for pupils, parents, staff and the local community. We check that the school meets the requirements set by the Department for Education, the Local Authority and Health and Safety Executive
The governors are allocated different responsibilities; all are linked to a particular class, and some governors have other areas of responsibility such as for a curriculum subject, Special Educational Needs or Safeguarding. Governors visit their link classes whenever possible, helping out and getting to know the children. Through meetings with the headteacher, staff and pupils, governors monitor the school’s performance and its school improvement programme.
We have a clerk to assist us in setting agendas, taking minutes and ensuring that the Governing Board fulfils all its statutory duties. If you would like to contact any of the governors please do so through the school office.
Neil Baker Chair of Governors

pageCache.pageTitle: Semley CE VA Primary School - Emergency closures
pageCache.text:
Emergency closures
In the event of the school closing due to adverse weather conditions, we will text parents to let them know, as well as posting information on the school website.
A decision to close the school is only taken after very careful consideration, and a number of factors will influence this.
We need to ensure the site itself is safe for children and consider whether we can provide sufficient staffing levels to enable adequate supervision of the children. A number of our staff live many miles from the school and we need to consider the safety of staff in travelling to school in relation to the roads around Semley and those further afield.
We will also keep a close eye on the weather forecast and in exceptional circumstances it may be necessary to close the school if the weather is expected to deteriorate. In making such a decision, we would take into account the potential need for parents to collect their children from school and then for staff to be able to get home safely afterwards.
